title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial formalism of 'figures', a combinatorial approach to tame topology. On p.15 he moves from the abstract structure (Fig, ≪) to a description 'in terms of M'. There the datum (1.33) is a family 𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(M) of subsets of a set M, together with an order ≤ on 𝓕 implied by inclusion.

Page 16 states the first axioms.

(i) For every x ∈ M, the set 𝓕^x of members F ∈ 𝓕 containing x has a smallest element F_x. 𝓕 thus defines a preorder on M: y ≤ x iff y ∈ F_x, so F_x = M_{≤x}.

(ii) The map x ↦ F_x is injective, i.e. 𝓕 separates points in the T0 sense. The preorder is then an order.

Consequences:
- Every F ∈ 𝓕 contains the M_{≤x} for x ∈ F, hence is a down-closed ('fermée') subset of the poset (M, ≤). This is the closed-set notion of the Alexandrov topology.
- He adds the axiom ∅ ∈ 𝓕, and remarks that this makes 𝓕 'never admissible', referring to a notion fixed earlier and not visible here.

He then recalls that GF IV (first version of Analysis situs) treated at length the equivalence between:
- abstract data (𝓕, ≤) satisfying conditions C1, C2, C3 (there §3, §4, §8; a marginal note says he rather called them Af1, Af2, Af3); and
- a poset M with a family 𝓕 of down-closed subsets containing all principal ideals M_{≤x} and ∅, satisfying a compatibility condition: if F, G ∈ 𝓕 and M_{≤x} ∪ M_{≤y} ∈ 𝓕 for all x ∈ F, y ∈ G, then F ∪ G ∈ 𝓕.

So 𝓕 is not a full topology. It is not closed under unions. Unions are admissible exactly when they are 'pairwise coherent' at the level of points. This is a flag/clique-type condition, as in flag complexes or Girard-style coherence.

The next page says this need not be revisited. He turns to 'shadows' (ombres), and to two test models: set-theoretic figures Fig(L), and finite affine simplicial figures over an ordered field. Figures 'of finite type' are defined as finite unions of M_{≤x_i}.
errors: Axiom (i) tacitly requires 𝓕^x ≠ ∅ for every x, e.g. M ∈ 𝓕 or M a union of members. This is not stated on the page.
The remark that ∅ ∈ 𝓕 makes 𝓕 'never admissible' depends on a definition of 'admissible' not visible here. As written it is cryptic rather than wrong.

The compatibility condition gives closure under unions only for pairwise compatible pairs. It does not by itself give closure under the binary unions that would be needed for, e.g., finite-type figures to form a lattice. This is fine as an axiom but should not be over-read.

ideas.what: Recovering an order on M from a family of subsets via least elements F_x, with T0 separation making the preorder an order
ideas.modern_name: Specialization preorder of an Alexandrov-type closure system; T0 condition

ideas.what: Family of down-closed subsets containing principal ideals and ∅, with a binary 'coherence' axiom: pairwise-compatible principal ideals imply the union is a figure
ideas.modern_name: Flag/clique-type closure condition; analogous to coherence spaces, Scott information systems and event structures, or flag simplicial complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Girard (coherence spaces, 1986–87); Scott (information systems, 1982); Winskel (event structures)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished GF IV / Analysis situs notes (Montpellier archive)

ideas.what: Equivalence between abstract figure data (𝓕, ≤) with axioms C1–C3 (Af1–Af3) and poset-with-admissible-down-sets data
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorem for an abstract 'figure' formalism by a poset of cells (cf. face posets, CW-posets)
ideas.where_published: Referred to as being in GF IV (first version), unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics of 'figures' on a poset has the same shape as Girard's coherence spaces and Scott-style information systems of the same years (1986–87). In both, admissible sets are down-closed, all principal ideals are admissible, and a pairwise-compatibility condition forces unions to be admissible. Here it is motivated by tame/combinatorial topology rather than by semantics of computation. The parallel seems not to have been remarked.
missed.quote: si F, G ∈ 𝓕, telles que ∀x∈F, y∈G on ait M_{≤x} ∪ M_{≤y} ∈ 𝓕, alors F∪G ∈ 𝓕. (condition de compatibilité)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links Grothendieck's unpublished 'Analysis situs' and tame-topology programme with domain theory and with flag-complex combinatorics. This could inform modern combinatorial models of stratified or o-minimal spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: The page mostly sets up routine order-theoretic axioms. The coherence-type union axiom, and the reference to a fully worked equivalence in the unpublished GF IV, are a modestly notable glimpse of an unknown formalism. The content itself is elementary.
transcription_corrections: Struck marginal fragment on p.16: the image suggests '(ii) (iii), vérifiant ... que ...' is part of a crossed-out line, not active text.
'ce qui implique que 𝓕 n'est jamais admissible !' — 'jamais' is underlined in the image; the reading is plausible.
Margin: 'J'appelais ces conditions plutôt Af 1, Af 2, Af 3' rather than 'je les appelais conditions plutôt'.
Section references read '§3, §4, §8' (the middle one is uncertain).
